name: Akekee
rangeDescription: Kauai (kokee and alakai swamp environs)
description: A small, very rare Hawaiian honeycreeper of remote native forests on Kauai. Declining rapidly; found only above 4,000 feet elevation in the eastern ‘Alaka’i Plateau.

name: Horned Guan
rangeDescription: Humid forest of southern mexico (chiapas) and guatemala
description: Large, long-tailed game bird restricted to undisturbed humid evergreen forest on a few high mountains in Guatemala and adjacent southern Chiapas, Mexico; very rare and local. Mainly found singly in forest canopy, where can be easily overlooked.

name: Red-billed Tyrannulet
rangeDescription: Foothills of eastern ecuador and eastern peru (southward to madre de dios)
description: Small and rather scarce flycatcher found in disturbed forest on the east slope of the Andes. Yellowish-olive with a gray head and pale throat.

name: Javan Owlet
rangeDescription: Java and bali
description: Chunky small owl with a big rounded head. Note finely barred head, bright chestnut back and wings, and white underparts marked with long brown streaks.

name: Vogelkop Melidectes
rangeDescription: Western new guinea (tamrau, arfak, fakfak, and kumawa mountains)
description: A fairly large honeyeater of mid-montane forest and edge. Black body with olive wing feathers, boldly patterned with white scales on the back, flanks and dappled white on the chest.

name: Galapagos Hawk
rangeDescription: Galapagos
description: Brown hawk endemic to Galápagos. Adult is quite dark and may appear nearly black in harsh light; also note white barring in wings and tail, and yellow at base of bill.

name: Ibisbill
rangeDescription: Rocky mountain streams and rivers of central asia
description: Expertly camouflaged amongst the fast-moving rocky rivers and streams it prefers, this specialized wader is often difficult to see. Upperparts are gray and faded brown; white belly is bound in by a black belt; a vaguely crescent-shaped black patch on the face is unique among waders.

name: Jamaican Owl
rangeDescription: Woodland of jamaica
description: A somewhat large nocturnal inhabitant of wooded areas including gardens and parks; roosts in tree cavities or dense foliage during the day. The Barn Owl is of similar size, but it is much paler and lacks the Jamaican Owl’s prominent ear tufts.

name: Philippine Cockatoo
rangeDescription: Forest and scrub of philippines including palawan
description: A rare large parrot of forest on Palawan and several other scattered islands. Heavily persecuted.

name: African Spoonbill
rangeDescription: Sub-saharan africa and madagascar
description: A distinctive pale waterbird with long pink-red legs, a bare bright pink-red face, and an odd and distinctive spoon-shaped bill that is obvious even in flight. The juvenile lacks the bright pink-red skin and has black tipped wings in flight.

name: Long-billed White-eye
rangeDescription: Mountains of pohnpei (eastern caroline islands)
description: Bizarre and unique-looking white-eye, endemic to Pohnpei, in Micronesia’s Caroline Islands. Pale brownish-olive overall, with orange legs and a long curved bill; the two other white-eyes on the island, Pohnpei White-eye and Caroline Islands White-eye, are gray and yellow respectively, and both have short bills.

name: Iiwi
rangeDescription: Ohia and mamane forest of main hawaiian islands
description: A bright red Hawaiian honeycreeper of high elevation native forests on Kauai, Maui, and Hawaii Island. Very rare on Oahu and Molokai.

name: Banded Whiteface
rangeDescription: Interior of central western australia to far southwestern queensland
description: Small bird with stubby bill, found in arid open areas across inland central and western Australia. Warm brown above, white below, with thin dark gray chest band, reddish-brown marks on the flanks, pale eye, whitish throat, and white mark above bill.

name: Mountain Buzzard
rangeDescription: Highlands of ethiopia to tanzania and malawi
description: Medium-sized brown raptor of montane habitats. Shows thick dark brown streaking on the underparts.

name: Lady Amherst's Pheasant
rangeDescription: Mountains of southeastern tibet and southwestern china to northern myanmar
description: Attractive terrestrial bird of hilly forests with dense patches of undergrowth. Stately male is resplendent, with long striped tail, white belly, and black-and-white scaling on neck.

name: Blue-eyed Ground Dove
rangeDescription: Cerrado of south-central brazil
description: Stunningly beautiful dove that has only recently been rediscovered. Cinnamon-colored overall but paler below.

name: Gorgeted Puffleg
rangeDescription: Serranía del pinche, southwestern cauca, colombia
description: Rare and endangered hummingbird found in the Andes of southwestern Colombia. Accessing its tiny known range is difficult, and only a few intrepid and lucky birders have seen one.

name: Bay-chested Warbling Finch
rangeDescription: Scrub of southeastern brazil (minas gerais to northern río grande do sul)
description: Small finch with a conspicuous chestnut breast and flanks. Gray above with a white throat and belly and a white arc below the eye.

name: Tahiti Swallow
rangeDescription: Moorea and tahiti (society islands, east-central polynesia)
description: Handsome swallow endemic to Tahiti and Moorea. Adult is iridescent blue above and smoky gray below, with an orangish throat and forehead.

name: Tickell's Thrush
rangeDescription: Himalayas of kashmir to nepal; winters to southern peninsular india
description: Both sexes of this thrush are fairly uniformly-colored: the male is predominantly blue-gray and the female is warm brown with a slight buffy wash to the underparts. May be confused with Indian Blackbird in southwestern wintering range, but both sexes are paler and smaller than their respective counterparts of that species.
